description: What will DRAM/NAND (and LPDDR5X/HBM) contract prices average in calendar 2026-2027, the memory input cost that Morgan Stanley says now makes up 25-30% of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin rack bill of materials?
outcome: The trajectory of memory contract prices for 2026-2027, and whether the memory cost surge reflected in ~$2 million of memory content per Vera Rubin rack (a 435% jump) persists, eases or worsens — moving NVIDIA's rack BOM cost, rack pricing and gross margin.
period: Calendar years 2026-2027 — checked against TrendForce/DRAMeXchange quarterly DRAM/NAND contract price releases and memory makers' reported contract prices/ASP, since the item ties 'sharply' higher contract DDR5 pricing and the ~$2 million/rack memory content to the Vera Rubin build ramping Q3-Q4 2026.

description: What will the spot rental price for an hour of Nvidia H100 GPU compute average over calendar 2026, versus the roughly $3.20-an-hour peak reached in May 2026?
outcome: The calendar-2026 average spot price for an hour of H100 GPU time on compute marketplaces, compared with the ~$3.20/hour May 2026 peak.
period: Calendar 2026; settled by full-year 2026 H100 spot rental price data published after year-end 2026 (the quantity is for the current calendar year, per the item's 'over the last year' series).

description: What will the average contract price of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) be in calendar 2026, after memory makers raised prices tenfold over the past year?
outcome: The average HBM contract price for calendar 2026 (or Q4 2026), versus the tenfold increase over the past year cited by TechCrunch.
period: Calendar 2026; settled by the Q4 2026 HBM contract price release (TrendForce/DRAMeXchange or Micron's fiscal Q4 2026 report), the release date of the quantity. The item does not give a release date, so the check date is the end of the calendar year it covers.

description: How much will contract prices for the DRAM/DDR5 memory that dominates the bill of materials of AI server racks rise in calendar 2026, as tight DRAM, NAND and HBM supply meets AI-driven demand?
outcome: The change in contract DDR5 (DRAM) prices in calendar 2026 versus 2025, the memory input that now accounts for roughly a quarter or more of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin rack value.
period: Calendar 2026 — checked against TrendForce/DRAMeXchange quarterly DRAM contract price data, with the Q4 2026 release settling the full-year change (release date fixes the check).

description: How much will NVIDIA have invested in, and hold as equity in, Firmus Technologies by the time of Firmus' ASX listing later in 2026, after subscribing for about US$500 million of preference shares in the neocloud's US$2 billion equity raising?
outcome: The final size of NVIDIA's ~US$500 million subscription for Firmus preference shares and their conversion into ordinary Firmus equity at the ASX IPO.
period: Firmus' ASX listing later in 2026 (check date 2026-12-31, set from the item's statement that the IPO is later this year); NVIDIA's next annual report should also disclose the stake's carrying amount.

description: What will contract DRAM and NAND memory prices be for calendar 2026, given the AI-driven supply squeeze now embedding sharply higher memory cost in AI systems?
outcome: The direction and magnitude of 2026 contract DRAM/NAND (including LPDDR5X and HBM-adjacent) prices versus the prior year as AI data-center demand absorbs supply — whether the squeeze keeps pushing memory prices up (the item cites a 435% rise embedded in NVIDIA's next rack and sharply higher contract DDR5 pricing) or eases.
period: Calendar 2026 — checked against memory-market contract price releases (e.g., TrendForce/DRAMeXchange quarterly DRAM and NAND contract prices) through year-end 2026.

description: What will the spot rental price of an Nvidia H100 GPU-hour be in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026, after the roughly $3.20/hour peak in May 2026?
outcome: The Q4 2026 average H100 GPU-hour spot rental rate on compute marketplaces such as Ornn, compared with the ~$3.20/hour May 2026 peak.
period: Q4 calendar 2026; set from the item's 12-month H100 spot-price series published 2026-07-09, measured in Ornn's Q4 2026 data release (January 2027).

description: What will the spot rental price for an hour of NVIDIA H100 GPU compute be at the end of calendar 2026, versus the roughly $3.20 an hour peak reported in May 2026?
outcome: The year-end 2026 level of the spot price for an hour of H100 GPU time published by compute marketplaces such as Ornn, compared with the May 2026 peak of about $3.20/hour and the subsequent decline.
period: 2026-12-31 (year-end reading of the continuously published Ornn H100 spot-price index; the item reports a May 2026 peak of ~$3.20/hour followed by a steady drop-off but gives no future date, so the check date is set at the end of the calendar year the data cover).

description: How much will Google, Amazon, Microsoft and OpenAI spend in aggregate on their own custom AI processors in calendar 2026, as they try to reduce dependence on Nvidia?
outcome: Combined calendar-2026 spending by Google, Amazon, Microsoft and OpenAI on custom AI accelerators/ASICs, as disclosed or estimated.
period: Calendar 2026; settled by the four companies' Q4 2026 earnings disclosures or capex/accelerator spending breakdowns (January-February 2027), the release date of the quantity.

description: Where will US export-control policy on NVIDIA AI-chip sales to China stand at NVIDIA's fiscal year-end 2027 — will the US maintain the current conditional approval for some sales, broaden it, or re-tighten restrictions?
outcome: The state of US export-control permission for NVIDIA AI-chip sales to China as of NVIDIA's fiscal year-end 2027, as reflected in Commerce/BIS decisions and license approvals.
period: NVIDIA fiscal year ending late January 2027 (reported ~February 2027); set as the current fiscal year-end for an evolving regulatory stance the item reports as in force.

description: What will DRAM and high-bandwidth memory prices be at the end of calendar 2026, after memory makers raised prices roughly tenfold over the year to July 2026?
outcome: The year-on-year change in the DRAM/HBM price in Q4 calendar 2026 versus Q4 2025.
period: Q4 calendar 2026; set from the item's 12-month memory-price series published 2026-07-09, measured in the Q4 2026 price releases published in early 2027.

description: How much will NVIDIA hold in Firmus Technologies' equity, and at what total committed amount, at NVIDIA's next annual report, following its reported subscription for about US$500 million of Firmus preference shares in Firmus's US$2 billion raise?
outcome: The size and carrying value of NVIDIA's equity stake in Firmus Technologies (preference shares designed to convert to ordinary equity at Firmus's ASX IPO), as disclosed at NVIDIA's next annual report.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K, expected early 2027); the investment is reported as undertaken, so it is tracked by its amount at the next annual report.

description: Where will the spot price for an hour of H100-class GPU compute be at the end of calendar 2026, versus its ~$3.20/hour peak in May 2026, as custom AI accelerators from NVIDIA's largest customers pressure compute pricing?
outcome: The spot hourly rental price for an H100 GPU on compute marketplaces at end-2026, versus its May 2026 peak.
period: 2026-12-31 (end of calendar 2026; the check date for the spot H100 GPU-hour rate against its ~$3.20 May 2026 peak).

description: What share of Chinese companies' AI accelerator budget will go to domestic products over the 12 months following the July 2026 Bloomberg Intelligence survey, versus executives' planned 46% (up from 30%)?
outcome: Domestic suppliers' realized share of surveyed Chinese companies' AI accelerator budget allocations over the 12 months from July 2026.
period: 12 months from the July 2026 survey (to about July 2027); settled by a follow-up survey or China AI accelerator market-share data released around mid-2027.

description: How much will NVIDIA have invested in Firmus Technologies, and what will its Firmus equity stake be carried at, at NVIDIA's next annual report, following its subscription for roughly $500 million of Firmus preference shares that convert to ordinary equity at Firmus's ASX IPO?
outcome: The dollar amount NVIDIA discloses as invested in Firmus Technologies and the carrying value of its resulting Firmus equity stake, versus the roughly $500 million subscription reported here.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K, expected early 2027); the subscription is undertaken, so it is tracked by its amount at the next annual report.

description: Will DRAM/HBM spot prices be higher or lower at the end of calendar 2026 than in mid-2026, after roughly tenfolding over the prior year as data-center memory demand outpaces supply?
outcome: The change in DRAM spot prices from mid-2026 to end-2026.
period: 2026-12-31 (end of calendar 2026; the check date for the change in DRAM spot price versus mid-2026).

description: How much will U.S. federal agencies obligate in AI spending in 2026, versus the $7.2 billion reported as reached in 2026?
outcome: The final total of U.S. federal AI spending obligations for 2026.
period: 2026 (full-year 2026 data; check date 2026-12-31, set from the item's 2026 figure).

description: How much will U.S. federal agencies obligate on AI-related spending in calendar 2026, versus the $7.2 billion already obligated and the $91.8 billion of potential contract awards reported as of mid-2026?
outcome: Full-calendar-2026 federal AI spending obligations (and the value of AI-related contract awards in the pipeline), compared with the $7.2 billion of 2026 obligations and $91.8 billion of potential awards reported in this item.
period: Calendar 2026 (to 2026-12-31), the year the item's obligation and award figures cover; settled by full-year federal AI obligation/award data published after year-end 2026.
